- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope afterward.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term upside; cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model exhibits lagged reactions; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized in model — if price is >15% above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 2–4% per week until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward corrections after negative sentiment; add 1–2% buffer below true outcome if sentiment <0.4 for 3+ consecutive days.
